# Infrastructure Plan Report — Startup (3-Developer Team)

## How We Understood Your Request
You described a 3-developer team building a startup app with 3 services. We classified this as an **early-stage/seed-stage startup** — moving fast and cheap, not yet building for scale or compliance. Key inferences:

- **Traffic:** Low-to-moderate (dev/test + early users) — no traffic figures were given, so this was inferred from team size, not assumed enterprise-scale.
- **Environments:** dev + prod only (no separate staging — a 3-person team typically doesn't have dedicated QA).
- **Compliance:** None assumed — no fintech/healthcare/government signals in your request.
- **High availability / Multi-AZ:** Not required — traffic and budget at this stage don't justify the added cost.
- **Budget sensitivity:** High — architecture favors cost-efficient, minimal footprint over redundancy.
- **Region:** Defaulted to us-east-1 (cheapest/most common AWS default, since none was specified).

Please flag if any of these assumptions are wrong (especially traffic volume or compliance needs) — they drive most of the cost and complexity decisions below.

## What Was Scoped, and Why
A single shared EKS cluster (namespace-isolated, not per-environment) runs all 3 services — cheaper than separate clusters at this scale. Each service gets its own ECR repo, CI/CD pipeline, and Kubernetes deployment for independent releases. Networking is kept to the minimum AZ count required by the load balancer, not full multi-AZ redundancy. A shared ALB exposes all services instead of provisioning one load balancer per service. Basic IAM roles (per-developer, CI/CD, node role), a Terraform remote-state backend, and baseline CloudWatch monitoring round out the setup — enough to operate safely without over-engineering.

## What Was Explicitly Excluded, and Why
- **Multi-AZ HA & multi-region DR** — not justified by current traffic/budget.
- **Compliance tooling** (AWS Config, org-wide CloudTrail, GuardDuty) — no regulated data indicated.
- **Separate staging environment** — team size doesn't support a dedicated QA stage yet.
- **Per-environment dedicated clusters** — unnecessary cost at this scale.
- **WAF/advanced security tooling** — not indicated as high-exposure public-facing traffic.

These are the first things to revisit as you grow (more users, funding, compliance triggers, or team size).

## Turnaround
- **Manual estimate:** ~15 person-days of engineering/architecture time.
- **Agent-assisted:** ~25 minutes end-to-end (planning + generation + validation).

## Self-Correction Built Into the Pipeline
The generation stage runs `terraform validate`/`plan` and `kubectl` dry-run checks across all 16 provisioning steps before anything is presented as final — this is an automated safeguard, not a one-shot script dump, so structural errors are caught and corrected pre-delivery rather than discovered during your own deployment.
